report:
**Conclusion:** For most people, regularly taking vitamin C does **not** meaningfully prevent getting common colds. A Cochrane review of 29 trial comparisons (11,306 participants) found no reduction in cold incidence in the general population, so routine high-dose supplementation for prevention is not justified.

There is a limited exception: people undergoing brief, intense physical stress (for example, marathon runners or soldiers in very cold conditions) had fewer colds in the reviewed trials. Regular supplementation may also make a cold modestly shorter and less severe—about **8% shorter in adults** and **14% in children**—but starting vitamin C only after symptoms begin has not shown consistent benefit.

A balanced diet generally supplies adequate vitamin C; avoid assuming that large doses are harmless or necessary.

Sources:  
- https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD000980_vitamin-c-preventing-and-treating-common-cold  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23440782/  
- https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminC-HealthProfessional/
